correctness.rationale: For p>5, smoothness follows from the five-sign gradient argument; the 15 diagonal and 12 fifth-root lines exhaust 27. In nonsplit fields Galois mates among the 12 are skew by Fourier-vector independence, so rational points lie only on 15 diagonal lines. Their strongly regular incidence matrix has rank six, yielding Picard trace five; point multiplicities 10 triples and 15 doubles yield N0=\(Q^2-10Q+21\). The tangent-plane quadratic form independently proves that the only Eckardt points are the ten sign-pair points in every characteristic greater than five. In split fields classical 27-line pair incidence yields N0=\(Q^2-20Q+99\), and trace seven. The full finite-extension and zeta formulas follow algebraically. Exact rational incidence and six exhaustive finite-prime field verifiers executed successfully; those checks are not substituted for the general proof.

The nonsplit Frobenius and incidence computation gives its full extension counts and distinguishes the arithmetic types in a way not provided by the preexisting split formula.
